claims.text: MEASURED: of the 20 hits my surface detector found on ARM-08's gate, only 4 were CODE identifiers — 12 were string literals and 4 were comments. It fired, but 80% of its evidence was prose. Detecting THIS implementation is not the same as detecting AN implementation: a functionally identical gate that never spells 'adjust_counter' in its wording would have been invisible, and the control would have reverted to the false absence fixed one commit earlier.

Tokens broadened from the effect's English name to the SHAPE an authority gate takes: AdmitCounterWrite, EAdmission, CounterAuthority, bA2Writable, A2Writable, IsKnownCounter. Against ARM-08's tree the scan goes from 20 hits to 72, now anchored on API surface rather than comment text.

Broadening a detector usually costs precision, so the opposite direction was checked rather than assumed: against my own worktree, where no gate exists, the scan reports 0 occurrences and the control still exits 2 PRODUCT_AUTHORITY_PATH_ABSENT. The honest absence finding is intact and the suite is unchanged at exit 2.

tests.command: python3 test_e11_admission_path.py  # ARM-08 tree, broadened tokens
python3 Design/tests/test_e11_admission_path.py  # own worktree, must stay 0 hits

risks: The structural tokens are drawn from ARM-08's actual API, so the detector is now fitted to the one implementation that exists. That is better than fitting to its comments, but it is still fitted. A second, differently-shaped implementation would need its own tokens — the honest framing is 'detects the gates we know about', not 'detects any gate'.

A static token scan can only ever say a gate is PRESENT, never that it WORKS. The control is explicit that a present gate is UNEXERCISED; nothing here brings K-01C closer to exercising the C++ path, which still needs a built editor.
